subject: SCI
title: Earth & Space / Environmental Science
description: A capstone lab science built on the NGSS high-school Earth and Space Science performance expectations plus the environmental (human-impact and engineering) expectations. Students move from the life of stars and the origin of the elements to plate tectonics, Earth's climate system, natural hazards and resources in California, ecosystems and biodiversity, pollution, climate change, and engineering for sustainability, ending with an independent local environmental investigation. Every week includes a hands-on investigation with household materials or real NASA/USGS/NOAA data.
framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (HS Earth and Space Sciences, HS-LS2/LS4 human impacts, HS Engineering Design); 2016 California Science Framework; California Environmental Principles and Concepts

standards.HS-ESS1-1: Develop a model based on evidence to illustrate the life span of the Sun and the role of nuclear fusion in releasing energy that reaches Earth as radiation.
standards.HS-ESS1-2: Construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on astronomical evidence of light spectra, motion of distant galaxies, and composition of matter in the universe.
standards.HS-ESS1-3: Communicate scientific ideas about the way stars, over their life cycle, produce elements.
standards.HS-ESS1-4: Use mathematical or computational representations to predict the motion of orbiting objects in the solar system.
standards.HS-ESS1-5: Evaluate evidence of the past and current movements of continental and oceanic crust and the theory of plate tectonics to explain the ages of crustal rocks.
standards.HS-ESS1-6: Apply scientific reasoning and evidence from ancient Earth materials, meteorites, and other planetary surfaces to construct an account of Earth's formation and early history.
standards.HS-ESS2-1: Develop a model to illustrate how Earth's internal and surface processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales to form continental and ocean-floor features.
standards.HS-ESS2-2: Analyze geoscience data to make the claim that one change to Earth's surface can create feedbacks that cause changes to other Earth systems.
standards.HS-ESS2-3: Develop a model based on evidence of Earth's interior to describe the cycling of matter by thermal convection.
standards.HS-ESS2-4: Use a model to describe how variations in the flow of energy into and out of Earth's systems result in changes in climate.
standards.HS-ESS2-5: Plan and conduct an investigation of the properties of water and its effects on Earth materials and surface processes.
standards.HS-ESS2-6: Develop a quantitative model to describe the cycling of carbon among the hydrosphere, atmosphere, geosphere, and biosphere.
standards.HS-ESS2-7: Construct an argument based on evidence about the simultaneous coevolution of Earth's systems and life on Earth.
standards.HS-ESS3-1: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the availability of natural resources, occurrence of natural hazards, and changes in climate have influenced human activity.
standards.HS-ESS3-2: Evaluate competing design solutions for developing, managing, and utilizing energy and mineral resources based on cost-benefit ratios.
standards.HS-ESS3-3: Create a computational simulation to illustrate the relationships among management of natural resources, the sustainability of human populations, and biodiversity.
standards.HS-ESS3-4: Evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.
standards.HS-ESS3-5: Analyze geoscience data and the results from global climate models to make an evidence-based forecast of the current rate of global or regional climate change and associated future impacts to Earth systems.
standards.HS-ESS3-6: Use a computational representation to illustrate the relationships among Earth systems and how those relationships are being modified due to human activity.
standards.HS-LS2-6: Evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that complex ecosystem interactions maintain relatively consistent numbers and types of organisms in stable conditions, but changing conditions may result in a new ecosystem.
standards.HS-LS2-7: Design, evaluate, and refine a solution for reducing the impacts of human activities on the environment and biodiversity.
standards.HS-LS4-6: Create or revise a simulation to test a solution to mitigate adverse impacts of human activity on biodiversity.
standards.HS-ETS1-1: Analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints for solutions that account for societal needs and wants.
standards.HS-ETS1-2: Design a solution to a complex real-world problem by breaking it down into smaller, more manageable problems that can be solved through engineering.
standards.HS-ETS1-3: Evaluate a solution to a complex real-world problem based on prioritized criteria and trade-offs, including cost, safety, reliability, aesthetics, and social, cultural, and environmental impacts.
standards.HS-ETS1-4: Use a computer simulation to model the impact of proposed solutions to a complex real-world problem with numerous criteria and constraints.

units.title: Stars and the Origin of the Universe
units.big_idea: Light from distant objects reveals how the universe began, how stars shine, and where the elements came from.

units.title: Earth's Formation and History
units.big_idea: Rocks, meteorites, and other planets record Earth's 4.6-billion-year story.

units.title: Earth's Dynamic Systems and Plate Tectonics
units.big_idea: Heat from Earth's interior and water at its surface continuously reshape the planet, and changes in one system cascade through others.

units.title: Weather, Climate, and the Coevolution of Earth and Life
units.big_idea: Earth's climate depends on energy balance and the carbon cycle, and life has changed Earth as Earth has changed life.

units.title: Natural Hazards and Resources in California
units.big_idea: Where people live and how they use energy and minerals are shaped by hazards and resources, and every resource choice has costs and benefits.

units.title: Ecosystems and Biodiversity
units.big_idea: Biodiversity supports ecosystem stability, and human resource use can protect or erode it.

units.title: Water, Air, and Pollution
units.big_idea: Pollutants move through connected Earth systems, and technology can reduce their impact.

units.title: Global Climate Change
units.big_idea: Data and models show that human activity is changing climate at an unprecedented rate, with regional impacts in California.

units.title: Engineering for Sustainability
units.big_idea: Engineering design breaks global challenges into solvable problems with criteria, constraints, and trade-offs.

units.title: Capstone: Local Environmental Investigation
units.big_idea: Scientists answer local questions with data and communicate findings to their community.

objectives: Model nuclear fusion in the Sun's core
Explain how solar energy reaches Earth

days.title: The Sun's layers
days.work: Read about the Sun's structure and build a cross-section clay model labeling core, radiative zone, convection zone, photosphere, and corona.

days.title: Fusion model
days.work: Model the proton-proton chain with clay balls (protons/neutrons) showing 4 H → 1 He; calculate the mass lost and energy released with E = mc².

days.title: Observe sunspots
days.work: Build a pinhole projector and safely observe the Sun's disk; compare with today's NASA SDO image and sketch sunspots.

days.title: Sun's life span
days.work: Use the Sun's mass, luminosity, and fusion rate to estimate its main-sequence life (~10 billion years) and draw a model of its future (red giant, white dwarf).

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a CER explaining how energy from fusion in the core reaches Earth and take a short quiz.

weeks.assessment: Fusion model and CER on solar energy transfer.

weeks.topic: Light, spectra, and the Big Bang
objectives: Explain redshift and cosmic background evidence

days.title: DIY spectroscope
days.work: Build a spectroscope from a CD and cardboard tube; compare spectra of an incandescent bulb, LED, and fluorescent light and sketch the lines.

days.title: Spectral fingerprints
days.work: Match unknown spectra to element spectra and explain how astronomers determine star composition.

days.title: Expanding balloon
days.work: Draw dots on a balloon, inflate it in stages, and measure distances between dots to model Hubble's law; graph velocity vs. distance.

days.title: Evidence for the Big Bang
days.work: Read about redshifted galaxies, the cosmic microwave background (COBE/Planck), and the H/He ratio; organize the three lines of evidence in a table.

days.title: Explanation
days.work: Write a 1-page scientific explanation of the Big Bang theory citing all three lines of evidence.

weeks.assessment: Big Bang explanation scored on evidence and reasoning.

objectives: Trace the life cycles of stars of different masses

days.title: H-R diagram
days.work: Plot 30 stars by temperature and luminosity on a Hertzsprung-Russell diagram and identify main sequence, giants, and white dwarfs.

days.title: Life cycles
days.work: Create a branching flowchart of low-mass vs. high-mass star life cycles.

days.title: Element factories
days.work: Color-code a periodic table by origin (Big Bang, fusion in low-mass stars, massive stars, supernovae/neutron-star mergers).

days.title: We are stardust
days.work: Trace the origin of 5 elements in your body (H, C, O, Ca, Fe) and write a short explainer for a younger audience.

days.title: Communicate
days.work: Present a 3-minute infographic or podcast on how stars make elements and take a quiz.

objectives: Apply Kepler's laws and Newton's gravitation to orbits

days.title: Kepler's first law
days.work: Draw ellipses with string and pins at different focus spacings; calculate eccentricity and compare with planetary orbits.

days.title: Kepler's second law
days.work: Use the PhET Gravity and Orbits simulation to show equal areas in equal times; explain why planets speed up near perihelion.

days.title: Kepler's third law
days.work: Graph T² vs. a³ for planets using NASA fact-sheet data and confirm the linear relationship; predict a moon's period.

days.title: Satellites
days.work: Use Newton's law of gravitation to calculate the orbital speed of the ISS and a geostationary satellite.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Take the Unit 1 test on the Sun, the Big Bang, stars, and orbits.

weeks.topic: Early Earth and the solar system's formation
objectives: Use meteorites and other planets as evidence for early Earth

days.title: Solar nebula
days.work: Read about the solar nebula hypothesis and draw a storyboard of accretion from dust to planets.

days.title: Crater lab
days.work: Drop marbles from different heights into a pan of flour topped with cocoa and measure crater diameter vs. drop height; relate to the Moon's ancient surface.

days.title: Meteorites
days.work: Examine NASA images of chondrites and explain why meteorites date the solar system to 4.56 billion years.

days.title: Radiometric dating
days.work: Model half-life with 100 coins or M&Ms (remove 'decayed' ones each round) and graph the decay curve; solve dating problems.

days.title: Account of early Earth
days.work: Write an evidence-based account of Earth's formation using meteorites, lunar rocks, and zircon crystals.

weeks.topic: Seafloor spreading and the ages of rocks
objectives: Analyze seafloor age and magnetic striping
Explain why oceanic crust is younger than continental crust

days.title: Continental drift
days.work: Fit cut-out continents together using fossil and rock-type evidence as Wegener did.

days.title: Magnetic striping
days.work: Model seafloor spreading by pulling two paper strips through a slit and marking alternating magnetic polarity bands.

days.title: Seafloor age map
days.work: Analyze the NOAA seafloor age map: measure distance vs. age from the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and calculate spreading rate in cm/yr.

days.title: Oldest rocks
days.work: Compare the ages of the oldest oceanic crust (~180 million years) and continental rocks (~4 billion years) and explain the difference using subduction.

days.title: Evaluate evidence
days.work: Write an evaluation of three lines of evidence for plate tectonics and take a quiz.

days.title: Relative dating
days.work: Apply superposition, cross-cutting, and inclusions to sequence events in 4 rock-layer diagrams.

days.title: Layer model
days.work: Build layered sand/paper strata in a clear cup, add a 'fault' and 'intrusion,' and have a family member determine the sequence.

days.title: Timeline
days.work: Build a 4.6-meter scaled timeline (1 mm = 1 million years) marking major events from Earth's formation to humans.

days.title: California's story
days.work: Read about how California was assembled (accreted terranes, Sierra batholith, San Andreas) and add its events to the timeline.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Take the Unit 2 test on Earth's formation and history.

objectives: Use seismic evidence to model Earth's layers

days.title: Seismic waves
days.work: Use a Slinky to model P-waves and S-waves; explain why S-waves cannot pass through liquid.

days.title: Shadow zones
days.work: Analyze a diagram of seismic shadow zones and infer the liquid outer core; draw Earth's layers to scale.

days.title: Convection lab
days.work: Heat water in a glass pan over a low flame and add drops of food coloring to observe convection cells; sketch and relate to the mantle.

days.title: Hot spots
days.work: Use Hawaiian island ages to calculate Pacific Plate speed and direction over the Hawaii hot spot.

days.title: Model
days.work: Draw a labeled model of Earth's interior showing how convection cycles matter and drives plates; take a quiz.

days.title: Boundary models
days.work: Model divergent, convergent, and transform boundaries with graham crackers on frosting; record landforms each produces.

days.title: Global patterns
days.work: Plot the last 30 days of M4.5+ earthquakes from USGS on a world map and outline plate boundaries.

days.title: San Andreas
days.work: Study the San Andreas transform fault and measure offset features (e.g., Wallace Creek) to calculate slip rate.

days.title: Cascadia & mountains
days.work: Compare Cascadia subduction (Mt. Shasta, Lassen) with the Sierra Nevada's uplift; map California's landforms by process.

days.title: Check
days.work: Draw an annotated California cross-section from the Pacific to Nevada showing plate processes; take a quiz.

objectives: Measure water's effects on erosion and weathering

days.title: Properties of water
days.work: Test water's high heat capacity by heating equal masses of water and sand under a lamp and recording temperature every 2 minutes.

days.title: Chemical weathering
days.work: Place chalk in water vs. vinegar and measure mass loss over 24 hours to model acid weathering of limestone.

days.title: Frost wedging
days.work: Fill a small plaster block's drilled hole with water, freeze/thaw it several cycles, and record cracking.

days.title: Stream table
days.work: Build a sand stream table in a baking pan; vary slope and flow rate and measure erosion and deposition.

days.title: Lab report
days.work: Write a full lab report on one investigation with variables, data table, graph, and conclusion.

days.title: Four spheres
days.work: Diagram interactions among geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere for a wildfire event.

days.title: Albedo lab
days.work: Melt ice cubes on black vs. white paper under a lamp and record melt time and temperature; relate to sea-ice feedback.

days.title: Volcanic feedback
days.work: Analyze temperature data after the 1991 Mt. Pinatubo eruption and explain the cooling effect of aerosols.

days.title: Dams and rivers
days.work: Analyze how a dam changes sediment, beaches, and ecosystems downstream (e.g., Matilija Dam) as a feedback chain.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Take the Unit 3 test on Earth's dynamic systems.

weeks.topic: Earth's energy budget and climate drivers
objectives: Model energy flow into and out of Earth
Explain Milankovitch cycles and other climate drivers

days.title: Energy budget
days.work: Label NASA's Earth energy budget diagram and confirm incoming and outgoing energy balance.

days.title: Greenhouse jar
days.work: Compare temperatures in a covered vs. uncovered jar under a lamp for 30 minutes and graph results; discuss limits of the model.

days.title: Greenhouse simulation
days.work: Use PhET Greenhouse Effect to vary greenhouse gas concentration and record equilibrium temperature.

days.title: Long-term drivers
days.work: Model Milankovitch cycles (eccentricity, tilt, precession) and match them to ice-age cycles in Vostok ice-core data.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write an explanation of how changes in energy flow at different time scales change climate; take a quiz.

objectives: Build a quantitative carbon cycle model
Measure carbon movement in a home experiment
materials: bromothymol blue (aquarium/pool kit) or red cabbage indicator

days.title: Reservoirs and fluxes
days.work: Build a box-and-arrow carbon cycle model with reservoir sizes (GtC) and annual fluxes from NASA/NOAA data.

days.title: CO₂ and water
days.work: Blow through a straw into indicator solution to watch it acidify; relate to ocean acidification.

days.title: Plants take up CO₂
days.work: Place Elodea in acidified indicator under light and in the dark; record color changes to show photosynthesis removing CO₂.

days.title: Human flux
days.work: Calculate the net yearly increase in atmospheric carbon and compare human emissions to natural fluxes using the Keeling Curve.

days.title: Model check
days.work: Revise your quantitative model to include human emissions and explain what happens to excess carbon.

objectives: Argue from evidence that life and Earth systems coevolved

days.title: Oxygen revolution
days.work: Read about cyanobacteria and the Great Oxidation Event; examine images of stromatolites and banded iron formations.

days.title: Rusting model
days.work: Place vinegar-soaked steel wool in a sealed jar to show iron consuming oxygen; relate to banded iron formation.

days.title: Land plants and soils
days.work: Trace how land plants changed weathering, soil formation, and atmospheric CO₂ during the Devonian.

days.title: Extinctions
days.work: Analyze the end-Permian and end-Cretaceous extinctions as Earth-system events affecting life.

days.title: Argument & test
days.work: Write an evidence-based argument on coevolution and take the Unit 4 test.

objectives: Explain how hazards have shaped settlement

days.title: Earthquake risk
days.work: Look up your address on Cal OES MyHazards; record earthquake, flood, fire, and tsunami risk.

days.title: Liquefaction lab
days.work: Fill a pan with saturated sand, place small weights on top, and tap the pan to model liquefaction; relate to the 1989 Loma Prieta Marina District damage.

days.title: Wildfire
days.work: Analyze CAL FIRE data on acres burned over decades and explain links to climate, fuels, and development in the wildland-urban interface.

days.title: Historical case
days.work: Research how a hazard (1906 San Francisco earthquake, 1862 Great Flood) changed where and how Californians built.

days.title: Household plan
days.work: Write a family emergency plan and supply checklist for your top two hazards.

weeks.assessment: Family hazard plan and case-study summary.

objectives: Explain how resource availability shapes human activity

days.title: Cookie mining
days.work: 'Mine' chocolate chips from cookies with toothpicks under a budget and calculate profit, land damage, and reclamation cost.

days.title: California gold and oil
days.work: Read about the Gold Rush and Kern County oil fields; explain how these resources shaped settlement.

days.title: Water resources
days.work: Map the State Water Project and Central Valley Project; explain how water availability shapes agriculture.

days.title: Groundwater
days.work: Analyze Central Valley subsidence data and explain the link to groundwater pumping during droughts.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write an explanation of how one resource shaped your region and take a quiz.

weeks.topic: Energy and mineral resource design solutions
objectives: Evaluate competing energy solutions by cost-benefit

days.title: Energy mix
days.work: Analyze California's in-state electricity mix from the California Energy Commission and compare to 10 years ago.

days.title: Compare sources
days.work: Build a spreadsheet comparing solar, wind, natural gas, geothermal, and nuclear on cost, emissions, land use, and reliability.

days.title: Lithium
days.work: Evaluate lithium extraction from the Salton Sea (geothermal brine) vs. hard-rock mining for EV batteries.

days.title: Home audit
days.work: Use your household utility bill to calculate monthly kWh and CO₂ and test one solution (LED swap, solar panel) with a cost-benefit ratio.

days.title: Decision memo
days.work: Write a one-page memo recommending an energy solution for a California town with justified cost-benefit reasoning.

days.title: Concept map
days.work: Build a semester concept map linking stars, Earth formation, plate tectonics, climate, and resources.

days.title: Data practice
days.work: Complete a data-analysis review set using graphs from each unit.

days.title: Practice test
days.work: Take a practice exam and target weak areas with CK-12 readings.

days.title: Lab review
days.work: Review your lab notebook and summarize the claim and evidence from five investigations.

days.title: Semester final
days.work: Take the Semester 1 final exam.

materials: meter stick or 1 m² string quadrat

days.title: Biodiversity
days.work: Define genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity and calculate a simple diversity index from sample data.

days.title: Quadrat survey
days.work: Mark a 1 m² quadrat in a yard, park, or vacant lot and identify and count all organisms using iNaturalist.

days.title: Keystone species
days.work: Analyze sea otter–urchin–kelp data from the California coast as an example of a keystone species.

days.title: Succession
days.work: Compare succession after a California wildfire with succession on new volcanic rock; draw a timeline.

days.title: CER
days.work: Write a CER evaluating the claim that stable ecosystems maintain consistent numbers of organisms, using kelp forest data.

weeks.assessment: Quadrat data and CER on ecosystem stability.

days.title: HIPPO
days.work: Learn the HIPPO threats (Habitat loss, Invasive species, Pollution, Population, Overharvesting) and sort 10 case examples.

days.title: California hotspot
days.work: Explain why the California Floristic Province is a biodiversity hotspot and list five endemic species.

days.title: Invasives
days.work: Investigate one California invasive (quagga mussel, Argentine ant, ice plant) and its ecological and economic effects.

days.title: Condor recovery
days.work: Analyze California condor population data from 1982 to present and identify which interventions worked.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a quiz and write a paragraph on which threat is most serious in your region.

objectives: Create a computational simulation of resource management

days.title: Fishing game
days.work: Play a 'tragedy of the commons' fishing game with crackers (fish reproduce each round) and record the population collapse.

days.title: Build the model
days.work: Build a spreadsheet model of a fish population with growth rate, carrying capacity, and harvest.

days.title: Test strategies
days.work: Test three harvest policies (fixed quota, fixed percentage, no-take zones) and graph population over 50 years.

days.title: Biodiversity solution
days.work: Revise the simulation to add a habitat corridor or marine protected area and measure its effect.

days.title: Report
days.work: Write a short report recommending a management strategy with simulation graphs as evidence.

objectives: Design and evaluate a solution reducing human impact on biodiversity
materials: native plant seeds or a pollinator plant
wood scraps for a bee hotel (optional)

days.title: Case study
days.work: Study the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing over the 101 Freeway and the criteria used to design it.

days.title: Define the problem
days.work: Choose a local biodiversity problem and write criteria and constraints for a solution.

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a solution (pollinator garden, bird-safe windows, native lawn replacement) with a sketch and budget.

days.title: Build/plant
days.work: Implement a small-scale version (plant native seeds, build a bee hotel, apply window decals) and document it with photos.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Take the Unit 6 test on ecosystems and biodiversity.

weeks.assessment: Solution design portfolio and Unit 6 test.

days.title: Your watershed
days.work: Use the EPA 'How's My Waterway' tool to identify your watershed and its listed impairments.

days.title: Water testing
days.work: Test tap water, a local stream or pond, and rainwater with test strips; record pH, nitrate, and hardness.

days.title: Eutrophication
days.work: Add a pinch of fertilizer to one of two jars of pond water and observe algae growth over the week (continue observations daily).

days.title: Filtration
days.work: Build a layered sand-gravel-charcoal filter and measure turbidity before and after filtering muddy water.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a watershed report connecting test results to land use; take a quiz.

days.title: Particle catchers
days.work: Coat index cards with petroleum jelly and place them in 4 locations (near a road, indoors, backyard, garage) for 3 days.

days.title: Smog in California
days.work: Explain how the Los Angeles basin's inversion layer traps pollutants; diagram ozone formation.

days.title: AQI data
days.work: Graph a month of AQI data from AirNow for your area and identify causes of high-AQI days (wildfire smoke, heat).

days.title: Count particles
days.work: Collect cards and count particles under a magnifier in a 1 cm² square; compare locations.

days.title: Report
days.work: Write a lab report on particulate levels by location with recommendations.

objectives: Evaluate a technology that reduces pollution

days.title: Waste audit
days.work: Weigh and sort your household's trash, recycling, and organics for the week and record in a spreadsheet.

days.title: Microplastics
days.work: Filter a sample of beach sand or laundry lint water through a coffee filter and look for microplastic fibers with a magnifier.

days.title: Composting
days.work: Start a small compost bin and explain how California's SB 1383 organic waste law reduces methane.

days.title: Evaluate technology
days.work: Evaluate a pollution-reduction technology (catalytic converter, scrubbers, Ocean Cleanup) using cost, effectiveness, and side effects.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Take the Unit 7 test on water, air, and waste.

weeks.assessment: Waste audit analysis and Unit 7 test.

objectives: Analyze temperature, ice, and sea-level data

days.title: Weather vs. climate
days.work: Compare one week of local weather to 30-year normals and explain the difference between weather and climate.

days.title: Temperature record
days.work: Graph NASA global temperature anomalies since 1880 and calculate the warming rate per decade for recent decades.

days.title: Ice and sea level
days.work: Graph Arctic sea-ice extent and global sea-level data; calculate rates of change.

days.title: Proxy data
days.work: Compare current CO₂ levels to 800,000 years of ice-core data and describe how unusual the current rate is.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a data-interpretation quiz.

days.title: How models work
days.work: Read how climate models divide Earth into grid cells and test them by hindcasting the past.

days.title: Scenarios
days.work: Compare low and high emission scenario projections for 2100 temperature and sea level.

days.title: Cal-Adapt
days.work: Use Cal-Adapt to project extreme heat days and snowpack for your county under two scenarios.

days.title: En-ROADS
days.work: Use the En-ROADS climate simulator to test policies and record which changes most reduce warming.

days.title: Forecast
days.work: Write an evidence-based forecast of climate impacts for your region in 2050 with uncertainty noted.

objectives: Connect climate change to drought, fire, snowpack, and coastline

days.title: Snowpack
days.work: Graph April 1 Sierra snowpack data and explain why it matters for California's water supply.

days.title: Weather whiplash
days.work: Analyze the swing from drought to atmospheric-river floods (e.g., 2022–2023) and its effects.

days.title: Sea-level model
days.work: Build a sand beach in a pan, add water, and model sea-level rise with melting ice to measure shoreline retreat.

days.title: Adaptation
days.work: Compare adaptation strategies (managed retreat, seawalls, groundwater recharge) for a coastal or valley community.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a quiz and write a paragraph on the climate impact you consider most urgent for your region.

objectives: Represent human modifications to Earth systems computationally

days.title: Footprint
days.work: Calculate your household carbon footprint with the EPA calculator and identify the three largest sources.

days.title: Reduction plan
days.work: Model in a spreadsheet how three changes would reduce your footprint over 5 years.

days.title: California policy
days.work: Read about AB 32, cap-and-trade, and the 2045 carbon-neutrality goal; summarize each.

days.title: Sequestration
days.work: Compare natural (forests, wetlands, soils) and technological (direct air capture) sequestration costs and capacities.

days.title: Unit 8 test
days.work: Take the Unit 8 test on climate change.

weeks.assessment: Footprint reduction model and Unit 8 test.

objectives: Specify criteria and constraints for a global challenge

days.title: Choose a challenge
days.work: Choose a global challenge (clean water access, urban heat, food waste) and research its scale with data.

days.title: Criteria and constraints
days.work: Write quantitative and qualitative criteria and constraints that reflect societal needs.

days.title: Decompose
days.work: Break the challenge into three smaller engineering problems with a problem tree diagram.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Brainstorm and sketch at least five possible solutions to one sub-problem.

days.title: Check-in
days.work: Present the problem definition and get feedback; refine criteria.

objectives: Design and test a prototype solution

days.title: Choose design
days.work: Use a decision matrix to choose the best design (example: a solar oven for clean cooking, a cool-roof model, or a water filter).

days.title: Build v1
days.work: Build version 1 of your prototype from household materials.

days.title: Test v1
days.work: Test the prototype with a data protocol (e.g., solar oven temperature every 5 minutes for an hour).

days.title: Iterate
days.work: Modify one variable and build version 2.

days.title: Test v2
days.work: Retest version 2 and compare performance with a graph.

objectives: Evaluate solutions using prioritized criteria and trade-offs
Use a simulation to model impact

days.title: Trade-offs
days.work: Score your solution on cost, safety, reliability, aesthetics, and social/environmental impact.

days.title: Scale it up
days.work: Build a spreadsheet simulation of the impact if 10,000 households adopted your solution.

days.title: Sensitivity
days.work: Change key assumptions in the simulation and report how results change.

days.title: Design brief
days.work: Write a 2-page design brief: problem, criteria, design, test results, trade-offs, and simulated impact.

days.title: Unit 9 presentation
days.work: Present your design in a 5-minute pitch and answer questions.

days.title: Question
days.work: Choose a local question (e.g., Does street tree cover lower surface temperatures? How clean is the creek after rain?).

days.title: Background
days.work: Find three credible sources on the issue and summarize what is known.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Write a procedure with variables, sampling locations, replicates, and safety plan.

days.title: Pilot
days.work: Collect pilot data and adjust methods as needed.

days.title: Approval
days.work: Present the plan in a conference for approval.

days.title: Field day 1
days.work: Collect data at your first set of sites, recording date, time, conditions, and photos.

days.title: Field day 2
days.work: Collect data at the second set of sites using identical methods.

days.title: Field day 3
days.work: Collect replicate data to strengthen reliability.

days.title: Organize
days.work: Enter data in a spreadsheet, calculate means, and note measurement uncertainty.

days.title: Graph
days.work: Create graphs that answer your question and draft initial findings.

objectives: Analyze data and propose a local solution

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Interpret patterns in the data and state whether evidence supports the hypothesis.

days.title: Propose
days.work: Propose a local solution with trade-offs evaluated against criteria.

days.title: Write
days.work: Write the capstone report (introduction, methods, results, discussion, recommendation).

days.title: Stakeholder letter
days.work: Write a letter to a city council member, school, or water district sharing your findings.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Create a science-fair-style poster or slide deck.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present your capstone to family, co-op, or a local group and answer questions.

days.title: Review S2
days.work: Review Units 6–9 with a concept map linking biodiversity, pollution, climate, and engineering.

days.title: Practice test
days.work: Take a practice final exam and correct errors.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take the cumulative final exam.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a reflection on the most important environmental action you will take as an adult.
